### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s).

**30** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87330e8959070c0e0a18d1a48981c981642926b7`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `userId (5 routes)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87330e8959070c0e0a18d1a48981c981642926b7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d689aadc3199993f46d4fd16312fd993cb83c72b` — the merge of head `147b8876c778617d6728e3d8791659225446e5f3` into base `87330e8959070c0e0a18d1a48981c981642926b7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d689aadc3199993f46d4fd16312fd993cb83c72b && git checkout d689aadc3199993f46d4fd16312fd993cb83c72b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 87330e8959070c0e0a18d1a48981c981642926b7 147b8876c778617d6728e3d8791659225446e5f3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 87330e8959070c0e0a18d1a48981c981642926b7 && git merge --no-ff 147b8876c778617d6728e3d8791659225446e5f3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87330e8959070c0e0a18d1a48981c981642926b7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 87330e8959070c0e0a18d1a48981c981642926b7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The environment-side sign-in page (ui/apps/console ssoCallbackRefusal.ts, acceptance 3) goes to a follow-up card for the ui lane.

## Review — PASS

Head: `b6957df807cb9361c8915a96fffe8f3829d1501c` · reviewer: review#3 (`session_016WV4d1PGptBW3QRQNmy5e6`) · area A1 · Part of #32992

- **The refusal decision is untouched.** The D5.1 gate in `globalBeforeHook` still decides with `oidcAuthorizeGate({ userId, clientId })`. Only how the refusal is delivered moves to `answerRefusedAuthorization`. Anything that is not a page navigation (`isPageNavigation`, the same predicate as the mobile hand-off) still gets the thrown `APIError('FORBIDDEN', { code: 'ENV_ACCESS_DENIED' })` with the same message. The Console's `fetch`, bearer clients and `curl` are pinned byte-identical.
- **The short-circuit is real.** Returning a `Response` from the global before-hook ends the request before the vendor's authorize handler: the real-`AuthManager` pin asserts `302`, `no-store`, and `location` without `code`, and the allowing-gate CONTROL gets a code at the same URI. A refused navigation therefore never mints a code.
- **No open redirect.** The redirect is followed only for a `GET` `response_type=code` with no request object, a client the provider's own `getClient` reads as present, enabled and allowed `authorization_code`, a `redirect_uri` equal to a registered one string for string, and a custom `validateRedirectUri` (when set) that also accepts it. That is strictly narrower than the provider's own rule (the loopback-port form gets the page, pinned). Any read failure gets the page. `state` and `error_description` go through `URLSearchParams`; `iss` per RFC 9207.
- **Page.** The email and both URLs are HTML-escaped. The page sets CSP `default-src 'none'`, `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `nosniff` and `no-store`. "Switch account" is the provider's `/oauth2/end-session` (pinned), and "Back to console" is `getConsolePageUrl('/')`.
- `Clause-②: no` holds: no input is accepted or refused differently, and API callers keep the envelope. A browser navigation now gets the RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1 error delivery instead of raw JSON as the page. `Metadata-protocol: none`, patch.
- nit N1: the page is English-only. It's fine as a fallback, since the RP redirect path covers the usual case. Worth one line on the ui follow-up card.
- nit N2: `isPageNavigation` treats `Accept: text/html` without Fetch Metadata as a navigation, so such a scripted client gets the `302` instead of the `403`. That is the OAuth-correct answer, but it's worth naming in the changeset's caller list.

CI was not complete when read (16:54Z: 21 success, 16 skipped, 12 in progress, none red); the ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head.
